title: Temptation
definition: Temptation is the enticement to distrust God and choose sin instead of faithful obedience.
summary: Temptation calls believers away from God, but Christ gives strength to resist.
christFocus: Jesus was tempted without sin and helps His people resist temptation through His Word, grace, and intercession.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Temptation often begins by questioning God's goodness, twisting desire, and promising life apart from obedience. It may come through the flesh, the world, or spiritual opposition.

Temptation itself is not sin, but yielding to it is. Scripture teaches believers to watch, pray, flee what is dangerous, resist the devil, and walk by the Spirit.

Jesus faced temptation and remained sinless. Because He overcame, He is able to sympathize with weakness and provide mercy and help to those who are tempted.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content: Many people feel defeated because they mistake temptation for failure or wait too long to resist it. Temptation matters because it gives believers both realism about danger and hope for help.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Do not negotiate with temptation. Bring it into the light, use Scripture, pray immediately, flee where needed, seek accountability, and look to Christ for mercy and strength.
